content: (Obligatory discussion thread for #job postings > Lean release notes editor volunteer , in case there are questions. Please don’t “apply“ here, but send me a DM.)
For the benefit of those reading #general but not #job postings: I’m looking for a new volunteer.
Hi, I have one question: approximately how many monthly volunteer hours is this expected to take?

Probably @Violetta Sim can comment best on that. I expect with AI assistance on the first draft, one to two hours per release (i.e. per month), possibly more depending on your appetite for attention to detail. If you happen to anyways keep close tabs on lean development and usually skim through the release notes anyways then less extra time.
yes, it did usually take me more than two hours, but that's because I needed more time to understand the changes, so the time was well spent anyway :)

Hi Joachim,

I saw your note that you are looking for a new volunteer for the Lean release notes editor role.

I’d be interested in helping with this. I’m currently learning Lean seriously and I usually keep track of Lean development, so this seems like a good way for me to contribute while learning more about the ecosystem.

I understand the expected workload is roughly 1–2 hours per release/month, with AI assistance for the first draft and some human editing/checking afterward. That sounds manageable for me.

A bit about me: I’m from Thailand, with CubeSat payload engineering experience, and I’m now focusing on Lean/formal methods. I’d be happy to start with a small trial task if that would be useful.

Best,
Pongsapak
Hi, Thanks for reaching out! We have a volunteer now, but will reach out again should they resign at some point.
